text:
sanjay: Quick brain-dump — noticed a bunch of evict/reload churn on tenant alpha during yesterday's load spike. Proposal: add a per-tenant eviction hysteresis (soft window) + QoS reservation so hot prefixes don't ping-pong. Thoughts?

jen: +1 on hysteresis, we saw same pattern in perf test. Curious on how long the window should be — too long and we waste memory, too short and we still oscillate.

mikayla: I think we should tie the window to observed inter-arrival for a prefix. e.g., hysteresis_ms = max( base, p50_interarrival * 3 ). That keeps it adaptive.

evan: Adaptive sounds good. Also need to avoid single-tenant hogs. We should expose a small reserved fraction per QoS tier (gold/silver/bronze) so gold gets guaranteed residency.

ira: Ops concern: longer hysteresis means more memory pressure during global spikes. How do we prevent OOM vs degraded latency?\
sanjay: tradeoffs: memory vs extra load. My thought: two-layer approach — per-tenant soft hysteresis + global emergency pressure that preempts hysteresis only when used_mem > global_threshold. So hysteresis is respected unless cluster is stressed.

jen: ok. How about demotion instead of full eviction? Move cold prefixes to a compact 'cold-slab' that keeps lightweight metadata and allows quick promotion. Demotion cost << reloading model KV.

mikayla: love demotion. We can store just a compressed token KV snapshot + last-seen timestamp. Promoting would be async fetch from cold-slab to fast-slab. Could be background warming.

evan: we need metrics to drive this: prefix_hits, prefix_misses, demotion_count, promotion_latency, tenant_residency_fraction. Also track interarrival_ms per prefix.

sanjay: Agreed. Proposed config proto (example):
```
eviction:
  base_hysteresis_ms: 5000
  adaptive_multiplier: 3
  global_pressure_threshold_pct: 0.82
  demotion:
    enabled: true
    cold_slab_retention_ms: 300000
  qos_tiers:
    - name: gold
      min_reserve_pct: 0.15
    - name: silver
      min_reserve_pct: 0.05
```

ira: nit: thresholds should be percent-of-usable-heap not raw memory. Also define what usable-heap excludes (cache metadata, runtime overhead).

mikayla: Implementation note: eviction decisions must be cheap on the hot path. Keep the hysteresis check as a single atomic timestamp + counter. Avoid locks.

evan: For multi-node sharing, need to make sure tenants with global affinity don't rehydrate simultaneously. Maybe add randomized backoff when promoting after demotion.

jen: Also consider lease-holder hints: if a prefix was recently write-active, prefer to keep it (reads can be reloaded). We can fold write_activity_score into eviction weight.

sanjay: Ops workflow: add alert when demotion_rate spikes > X/min and promote failures > Y. Also a synthetic test that blasts a tenant and checks global fairness.

infra-bot: perf-test/kv-hysteresis-canary started (run id: pt-2026-03-19-42).

mikayla: next steps I can spike the cold-slab prototype and instrumentation. Evan/jen — can you draft the QoS reserve semantics? I'll wire up metrics.

evan: yep, will draft semantics + API for reserve config.

jen: I'll write a short eval harness to simulate the ping-pong pattern with varying interarrival distributions.

sanjay: sounds good. Goal: land a small opt-in toggle behind a feature flag for Dedicated customers by end of sprint. If canary looks good, flip default later.

ira: one last thing — document rollback plan: feature-flag off + forced global GC.

mikayla: noted. I'll add that to PR.

sanjay: thanks all. TL;DR: per-tenant adaptive hysteresis + demotion cold-slab + QoS reserve + global emergency preempt. Spike, metrics, canary.
